features.method: Coordinate taken directly from the Hyper-Kamiokande Letter of Intent (arXiv:1109.3262), Section II.1, which states the site's own geographic coordinates and altitude. accuracy_m is set wider than a typical survey point (150 m rather than the ~20 m a minute/second-precision coordinate would normally warrant) because the LOI's figure was published in 2011 as the 'proposed location' before cavern excavation began (2022, per src:hk-frontiers-2024-status); no later source fetched this session restates numeric coordinates to confirm the final excavated position did not shift. The value is corroborated: it sits 346 m from the existing site record's own independently-derived point (offset-from-Super-K method), and 8.15 km from Super-Kamiokande's own surveyed point on a bearing of 177.8 deg (i.e. very nearly due south), matching the qualitative 'approximately 8 km south' stated in multiple Hyper-K status papers.
features.name: Hyper-Kamiokande cavern (surveyed point, Tochibora)

provenance.note: `verified` rests on `representation: surveyed` from a rank-10 arXiv technical paper (A15/A25), independent of any OSM check.
provenance.quote: at geographic coordinates Lat. 36 deg 21' 08.928'' N, Long. 137 deg 18' 49.688'' E, and an altitude of 508 m above sea level.

features.method: OpenStreetMap node 8719816444 (man_made=survey_point, natural=peak, name '池ノ山' [Ikenoyama], ele 1368.6 m), extracted via the maps.mail.ru Overpass mirror. A context feature only, drawn to show the mountain the Super-Kamiokande site's own summary already names ('under the peak of Mt. Ikenoyama'): this summit node is 153 m horizontally from Super-Kamiokande's own surveyed underground position, consistent with the detector sitting beneath it.
features.name: Mt. Ikenoyama summit (OSM survey point)

provenance.note: Context feature with no atlas entity of its own (entity_id null, per the contract's allowance for building/boundary/road/water-like context features); a mountain summit is not itself an accelerator, beamline, detector, site, experiment or facility.

features.method: OpenStreetMap node 759469233 (natural=cave_entrance, name 'Kamioka Mine, ICRR, Kamiokande, CLIO'), extracted via the maps.mail.ru Overpass mirror after overpass-api.de, lz4.overpass-api.de and the kumi mirror all refused connections this session. This node sits 1.87 km (bearing ~5.6 deg, i.e. almost due north) from Super-Kamiokande's own surveyed underground position — broadly consistent with the ~1.7-1.8 km horizontal Atotsu access tunnel described in secondary sources, though no primary source fetched this session states that tunnel length as a directly quotable figure, so this is reported as an informational corroboration in the worklog rather than a formal `checks[]` row.
features.name: Kamioka mine entrance (OSM cave_entrance node)

provenance.note: Marks a single named entrance to the Kamioka mine complex; OSM does not distinguish which of the mine's two named entrances (Atotsu, Mozumi) this node represents, and no source fetched this session resolves that.
provenance.quote: natural=cave_entrance, name='Kamioka Mine, ICRR, Kamiokande, CLIO'

features.method: Reuses the coordinate already recorded on site:kamioka-kamland verbatim (36.4225 N, 137.3153 E), itself the Wikipedia infobox value for KamLAND (rank 12); no additional computation is performed. No source fetched this session (the KamLAND overview arXiv:physics/0404071, the Antineutrino Science in KamLAND review arXiv:1409.4515, or the combined pre-supernova-alert paper arXiv:2404.09920) states a numeric distance-and-bearing offset from Super-Kamiokande precise enough to derive a better point; a WebSearch summary reports "500 m" but no fetched primary source states it, so it is not used (nothing from memory/unfetched summaries). accuracy_m matches the reused coordinate's own precision_m (2000 m) exactly, so this does not rest on a coarser anchor than its own claimed accuracy.
features.name: KamLAND (point, old Kamiokande cavity)

provenance.locator: Wikipedia infobox coordinate (36 deg 25' 21'' N, 137 deg 18' 55'' E)
provenance.note: Representation is honestly weak: the only fetched source is Wikipedia (rank 12), not a lab page or paper, so this is not `surveyed`, and it is not traced from OSM/GIS so it is not `georeferenced` either; `derived` is used here for a zero-offset reuse of the existing sourced parameter, flagged `approximate` confidence. See worklog backlog for a better source.

features.method: A 36-vertex circle of radius 19.65 m (half of the sourced 39.3 m tank diameter) computed on R = 6 371 008.8 m around the Super-Kamiokande detector's own surveyed GPS centre (36.425722 N, 137.310306 E, precision_m 50, from the SK NIM paper). accuracy_m is set to 50 m, equal to that surveyed anchor's own precision_m, per the coarse-anchor rule (a derived shape's accuracy_m may not be tighter than the anchor it rests on). This stands in for the detector tank footprint, not a trace of the excavated cavern itself (the cavern is larger than the tank; no source fetched this session gives the cavern's own dimensions).
features.name: Super-Kamiokande tank (derived circle, 39.3 m diameter)

provenance.locator: SK NIM paper (GPS survey of detector centre); Super-Kamiokande detector page, "39.3 m in diameter and 41.4 m in height"
provenance.note: Circle computed by this record's author from a sourced centre and a sourced diameter; not itself a published shape.
provenance.quote: at geographic coordinates 36 25' 32.6" N, 137 18' 37.1" E ... 39.3 m in diameter and 41.4 m in height

features.method: Great-circle line from the J-PARC accelerator complex's own surveyed/geocoder site coordinate (36.4587536 N, 140.5991750 E) to Super-Kamiokande's surveyed GPS coordinate (36.425722 N, 137.310306 E, the beamline's own far_detector_site_ids[0]), on R = 6 371 008.8 m. Drawn as the full baseline rather than truncated to a few kilometres (contrast geometry:cngs-direction-line) because both endpoints are themselves independently sourced site coordinates, which lets the geodesic length of this exact line be checked against the T2K instrumentation paper's own surveyed target-to-detector baseline (295,335.2 m) — not itself a physical structure, and clipped to the visible map extent by the browser like any other direction_line.
features.name: T2K neutrino beam, arriving from J-PARC (inferred direction)

provenance.locator: site:j-parc-main-ring's own sourced coordinate; SK NIM paper's GPS survey of the Super-Kamiokande centre
provenance.note: Not a physical structure: this is the T2K neutrino beam's direction, drawn on the far (Kamioka) end to show the direction from which it arrives. The validator recomputes the bearing from this line's first vertex (J-PARC) to beamline:j-parc-neutrino's far site (Super-Kamiokande, this line's own second vertex) and checks it matches.
provenance.quote: at geographic coordinates 36 25' 32.6" N, 137 18' 37.1" E, and altitude 370 m above the conventional (WGS-84) geodetic ellipsoid, as determined by a GPS survey

levels.name: Mt. Ikenoyama, Mozumi mine (~1000 m level)

depth_m.display: 650 m of rock at the detector centre

levels.name: Mt. Nijuugoyama, Tochibora mine (~650 m level)

map.name: Kamioka Observatory — Mozumi and Tochibora mines

summary.plain: The Kamioka Observatory's two underground sites in Gifu, Japan: the Mozumi mine, home to Super-Kamiokande and KamLAND, and the Tochibora mine 8 km south, where Hyper-Kamiokande is being built. Both receive the T2K neutrino beam from J-PARC, 295 km away.
